penalties.details: The order records that the appellate proceedings before the Commissioner of Income-tax (Appeals) [CIT(A)] resulted in partial relief on both issues. However, the consequential appeal-effect order pursuant to the CIT(A)'s decision has not yet been passed by the jurisdictional Assessing Officer. Accordingly, the penalty order notes that the penalty has been levied on a protective basis based on the assessment position presently available and is liable to be modified upon giving effect to the appellate order. The Company has already preferred further appeals before the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal in respect of the amounts / issues that continue to remain under dispute and is also pursuing consequential appeal effect before the jurisdictional tax authorities pursuant to the relief granted by the appellate order passed by the CIT(A). Based on its assessment of the matter, the Company believes that it has adequate grounds to contest the penalty order on merits and will continue to pursue the available appellate remedies. The order arises from tax adjustments/disallowances made during assessment proceedings and does not relate to concealment of income by the Company
penalties.impact: The financial impact of the order, as presently quantified, is Rs. 92.56 lakh, which remains subject to modification pursuant to the consequential appeal-effect order and the outcome of the pending appellate proceedings.

penalties.details: Penalty Order passed under Section 270A of the Income-tax Act, 1961 levying a penalty of ₹7,63 lakhs on Svara Hotels Limited, Subsidiary of the Company The penalty pertains to (i) disallowance of education cess deduction (penalty: Rs. 6.62 lakh), (ii) employees' PF/ESI contribution disallowance (penalty: Rs. 475), and (iii) disallowance of Section 80G deduction for donation to PM CARES Fund (penalty: Rs. 1.01 lakh). The first two matters arise from claims made based on the prevailing legal position, which were subsequently affected by retrospective legislative amendments. In respect of the PM CARES Fund donation, the claim was made with full disclosure of facts and supporting documentation, and the dispute relates to eligibility of deduction rather than concealment or misreporting. The Company believes it has a strong legal case and proposes to challenge the penalty order before the appropriate appellate authorities. As per prescribed procedure, the Company will deposit 20% of the demand while filing the appeals.
penalties.impact: Financial impact is limited to the penalty amount of ₹7,63,169 imposed under Section 270A of the Income-tax Act, 1961. .

timeline.summary: Arjun Singh Oberoi disclosed 1.15% (71,72,199 shares) in EIH Limited as of March 31, 2026, with no encumbrance.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹895.22 Cr (+8.2% YoY), net profit to shareholders ₹237.62 Cr (-6.1% YoY) (includes ₹19.72 Cr from discontinued operations; continuing operations ₹229.38 Cr).
Board of Directors recommended final dividend of ₹1.5 per equity share (75% of face value) for FY2025-26, subject to AGM approval on August 7, 2026, with record date July 31, 2026.
EIH Limited shared the recording link of its Investor Meet/Call held on 29th May 2026 via its website.
EIH Limited held its Q4 and FY26 earnings webinar on May 29, 2026, reporting record EBITDA and outlining expansion plans through 2030.
